doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Black players in Kenton's band and the 1953 Parker tour
summary: Konitz notes few black players in the band, and describes touring with Charlie Parker and Dizzy in 1953.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: I think so. The problem seemed to be that he didn’t have many black players coming through the band. There were some, Ernie Royal.
Not significantly enough for the black guys. I don’t know what disagreement Dizzy had with Stan but he really put him down strong.
But then later on in fifty-three Bird did that tour with the band, right?
Yeah. Dizzy was on that tour also.
Can you talk about that experience?
For me it was a big surprise when he asked me to do it and I asked who else was on it and he said Charlie Parker.
This was after you had left the band right?

Yeah. I exclaimed and I don’t remember ever hearing the reason for that, the justification for that. Why didn’t he get a tenor player like Stan Getz? The fact was that I was playing the arrangements I played when I was in the band and Bird was playing new arrangements and for whatever state his health was in he wasn’t terribly comfortable with Charlie Parker playing so I didn’t listen to him, usually. How do you like that? As Miles Davis kind of indicted when he was standing next to him, he couldn’t really hear him completely somehow because it was such a threat to him.
Miles said that he wanted to quit every night.
